content.thinking: Journal numbers aren't a reliable date proxy, so I need a better basis for the closed-period test. I'll check invoice 647's debit/credit mismatch, look for unbalanced journals, and look for postings made after close.

input.sql: SELECT "JRNL_NO", SUM("DR_AMT") dr, SUM("CR_AMT") cr FROM "GLJRNL" GROUP BY "JRNL_NO" HAVING SUM("DR_AMT")<>SUM("CR_AMT")
SELECT * FROM "SYSDICT" WHERE "TBL_NM" IN ('GLJRNH','GLPERD','APINVH') ORDER BY 1,2
SELECT * FROM "GLJRNL" WHERE "JRNL_NO" IN (2034,1629,2430,2431,2432) ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT a."INV_ID" a_id, b."INV_ID" b_id, a."VEND_CD", a."INV_NO", b."INV_NO", a."INV_AMT", a."INV_DT", b."INV_DT" FROM "APINVH" a JOIN "APINVH" b ON a."INV_ID"<b."INV_ID" AND TRIM(a."VEND_CD")=TRIM(b."VEND_CD") AND a."INV_AMT"=b."INV_AMT" AND (a."INV_DT"=b."INV_DT" OR regexp_replace(lower(a."INV_NO"),'-?[0-9]+$','')=regexp_replace(lower(b."INV_NO"),'-?[0-9]+$',''))
